summary: Pandora A/S (PNDORA.CO, NASDAQ Copenhagen) is a Danish jewellery manufacturer and retailer selling charm bracelets, rings, necklaces and earrings globally through owned concept stores, e-commerce and wholesale partners; in this Valuatum equity research report dated 30 July 2026 we rate the stock BUY with a 12-month target price of 1,112.30 DKK against a current price of 807.40 DKK, implying roughly 37.8% upside. Market capitalisation is DKK 60.4 bn and enterprise value is DKK 74.8 bn.

The core valuation tension is a stock trading at 6.70x 2026e EV/EBITDA versus its own 9.90x normalized historical average, a discount driven by tariff and commodity cost fears. Within the group, the market prices the Fuel with More growth segment at 9.1x EBITDA against a 0-1% like-for-like reality — giving it 37.2% of enterprise value on only 25.5% of revenue — while discounting Core's 6.1x cash engine too heavily given its resilient 22.7% EBIT margin. Margin defence hinges on a DKK 600m platinum-plating retool through 2026-2027 offsetting an estimated DKK 1.2bn annual tariff drag and record silver and gold costs, holding group EBIT margin at the 21-22% guided floor versus 23.9% in 2025.

On a reverse-valuation basis, closing the historical multiple gap on DKK 11,176m of 2026e EBITDA lifts the EV/EBITDA-based implied price to DKK 1,236.4, underpinning the blended 1,112.30 DKK target. The scenario base case of DKK 10,500m EBITDA at 6.9x implies DKK 729.11 per share, while re-acceleration of Fuel with More toward double-digit growth supports DKK 11,500m EBITDA at 8.0x and DKK 990.47 per share; if Core EBIT margin breaks below 20%, EBITDA falls toward the DKK 8,500m bear case at 5.5x and DKK 385.53 per share.

thesis.title: Fuel with More LFL growth needs re-acceleration
thesis.text: Fuel with More like-for-like growth collapsed to -3% in Q4 2025 before recovering to just +1% in Q1 2026; a re-acceleration toward high-single-digit growth is needed to justify its 27.6% EBIT margin and support the current 9.1x EV allocation embedded in the target.

thesis.title: Closing the valuation gap vs historical averages
thesis.text: The stock trades at 6.70x 2026e EV/EBITDA versus a 9.90x normalized historical average, a discount driven by tariff and commodity cost fears. Closing this gap on DKK 11,176m EBITDA lifts the EV/EBITDA-based implied price to DKK 1,236.4.

thesis.title: Platinum retool defends cash flow and margins
thesis.text: A DKK 600m platinum-plating retool through 2026-2027 must offset an estimated DKK 1.2bn annual tariff drag to hold group EBIT margin at the 21-22% guided floor, protecting cash flow and the blended valuation compared with 2025's 23.9% margin.

thesisBreaker: If Core EBIT margin breaks below 20% or Fuel LFL growth stays negative for two more quarters, EBITDA falls toward the DKK 8,500m bear case, collapsing implied equity value.

valuePools.name: Core (Moments/Charms)
valuePools.economics: Revenue DKK 24,249m (74.5%) · Comp. EBIT DKK 5,496m (70.6% of EBIT, 22.7% margin) · EV DKK 46,966m
valuePools.text: Profit engine generating DKK 24,249 million in annual revenue, 74.5% of the group total, with structurally robust modelled EBIT margins of approximately 22.7% and an estimated DKK 7,422 million in EBITDA, yet valued at a below-average normalized effective multiple of about 6.1x EBITDA as a mature harvest asset. The Moments platform's repeat-purchase replenishment stream fully funds network expansion, dividends (DKK 20.00 per share in 2025) and buybacks, but the cost structure faces record-high silver and gold prices and US import tariffs on Thai-made goods estimated at a DKK 1.2 billion annual gross headwind, prompting a manufacturing pivot to replace about 50% of pure silver pieces with platinum-plated alternatives by 2027.

valuePools.name: Fuel with More
valuePools.economics: Revenue DKK 8,300m (25.5%) · Comp. EBIT DKK 2,287m (29.4% of EBIT, 27.6% margin) · EV DKK 27,874m
valuePools.text: Scaling pool central to Pandora's 'Phoenix' strategy of moving beyond a single-category charm retailer into a full jewellery brand, generating DKK 8,300 million of FY2025 revenue at an estimated 82.8% gross margin, DKK 2,287 million of modelled EBIT (27.6% margin) and DKK 2,947 million of EBITDA. The market awards an implied premium multiple of roughly 9.1x normalized (13.0x raw) EBITDA on expansion into Modern Classics and Lab-Grown Diamonds — an LGD sub-segment sized at roughly USD 12 billion within the approximately USD 84 billion global diamond jewellery market. LFL growth decelerated to -3% in Q4 2025 and recovered to only +1% in Q1 2026, still far short of the double-digit growth needed to justify the premium multiple.

reverseValuation.intro: The reverse valuation tests whether the EBITDA, margin and multiple assumptions embedded in Pandora's enterprise value are coherent, with the scenarios diverging fundamentally on the progress of the DKK 600m platinum-plating strategy, the resulting volume resilience in the Core segment, and whether Fuel with More re-accelerates toward sustainable double-digit growth to prove out the Phoenix strategy's LGD ambition. Because Pandora carries DKK 17,912 million of net debt, equity value sits well below enterprise value and is heavily levered to the multiple applied.

coreAnalysis.heading: How the company creates economic value
coreAnalysis.text: Pandora's valuation rests on an enterprise-value control total of DKK 72,367 million allocated across two segments with very different economic profiles. Core (Moments/Charms), the vertically integrated accessible-luxury profit engine housing the legacy Moments platform and signature charm bracelets, produces DKK 24,249 million in revenue (74.5% of the group total) and an estimated DKK 7,422 million in EBITDA, yet the market allocates only 62.8% of group enterprise value to this mature segment, a normalized effective multiple of approximately 6.1x EBITDA. Fuel with More (Modern Classics and Lab-Grown Diamonds), by contrast, gets 37.2% of the enterprise-value allocation despite generating only 25.5% of group revenue and 28.4% of estimated EBITDA — an implied multiple of approximately 9.1x EBITDA that prices in the multiple expansion the Phoenix strategy is meant to deliver and needs sustained, robust growth to be justified.

coreAnalysis.heading: Cross-pool bridge
coreAnalysis.text: The forecast is anchored by Core's cash generation, which supports the balance sheet and funds the dividend, but the group EBIT trajectory (guided down to 21-22% for 2026 from 23.9% in 2025) is driven almost entirely by external factors: US tariffs on Thai manufacturing and the sharp rise in silver and gold prices. The bridge is weakest in 2026-2027, where the platinum-plating mitigation plan requires upfront capital spending estimated at DKK 600 million and carries execution risk before it delivers a structural margin defence. Using a normalized 9.9x EV/EBITDA multiple, the DKK 10,369 million in trailing EBITDA would in theory support the entire DKK 72,367 million enterprise value on an unlevered basis, which bridges to the DKK 54,455 million equity market capitalization by deducting DKK 17,912 million in net debt — leaving equity holders heavily levered to the success of Fuel with More. If Fuel with More were stripped of its growth premium and valued at the same ~6.1x multiple as Core, combined enterprise value would drop toward DKK 63,000 million; the valuation still holds up because Pandora generates large, recurring free cash flow, projected at DKK 5.4 billion in 2026, enough to de-lever organically and buy back shares.

coreAnalysis.heading: Scenarios and verdict
coreAnalysis.text: The scenarios differ mainly on the durability of gross margin and consumer reception to the brand's evolution, and the largest valuation swing comes from Core's gross margin: since Core drives nearly three-quarters of revenue, any structural inability to pass on silver costs or offset tariffs destroys EBITDA at a scale Fuel with More cannot make up for. The downside case depends almost entirely on the platinum-plating strategy failing — if consumers see platinum-plated jewellery as inferior to sterling silver, volumes would fall and break the retail network's operating leverage, with EBITDA toward DKK 8,500m at 5.5x implying DKK 385.53 per share. The upside requires Fuel with More to re-accelerate toward double-digit LFL growth, proving Pandora can capture a lasting, outsized share of the USD 12 billion Lab-Grown Diamond market and supporting DKK 11,500m EBITDA at 8.0x, or DKK 990.47 per share. The central investment debate is whether Pandora is a structurally declining charm bracelet retailer masking its maturity with financial engineering, or a more diversified, cash-generating jewellery platform successfully expanding into diamonds and modern classics: Core matters most for absolute cash generation and debt service, Fuel with More for valuation direction and multiple defence.

risks: Geopolitical / Tariff Implementation (Core (Moments/Charms)): US import tariffs on Thai manufacturing impose massive gross headwinds, with trade policy announcements as the early warning - HIGH impact, structural.

Commodity Inflation (Core (Moments/Charms)): structurally higher silver and gold prices compress gross margins before mitigation, with spot silver/gold prices as the early warning - HIGH impact, manageable.

Consumer Macro Environment (Core (Moments/Charms)): a K-shaped economy pressures middle-income discretionary spending, with store foot traffic declines as the early warning - MEDIUM impact, manageable.

Brand / Execution of Platinum Plating (Core (Moments/Charms)): consumer rejection of platinum-plated alternatives destroys unit volumes, with a decline in LFL volume mix as the early warning - HIGH impact and a thesis-breaker if it occurs.
catalysts: Fuel with More LFL growth trajectory (near-term, Fuel with More): a return to >5% LFL growth supports the 9.1x premium multiple; this quarter-by-quarter metric directly governs the multiple the market is willing to pay.
Platinum-plated volume mix adoption (medium-term, Core (Moments/Charms)): volume holding up while the product mix shifts defends the 21-22% EBIT margin floor.
US / Thailand tariff rulings update (near-term, Core (Moments/Charms)): confirmation of the tariff size (DKK 1.2bn) prevents further EBITDA drag.
EBIT margin progression over 2026 (medium-term, Core (Moments/Charms)): stabilization above 21% validates free-cash-flow generation.

faqs.q: How does the reverse valuation work for Pandora?
faqs.a: The reverse valuation tests the EBITDA, margin and multiple assumptions embedded in Pandora's enterprise value, with scenarios diverging on the DKK 600m platinum-plating strategy and Fuel with More's growth.
